messages.subject: WAIC
parts:
INLA offers the option to calculate WAIC. 

 

In other settings, I see WAIC calculated as the result of simulations from the posterior, with a standard error often provided to help determine whether differences in WAIC between models are meaningful (e.g., with the LOO package). 

 

INLA, however, reports a single WAIC value and a single series of WAIC values per observation. 

 

Is this because, as a deterministic system, there only is one possible WAIC value for an INLA posterior?  When I repeat the model run, the calculated WAIC value appears to be identical.

 

Or, should I be resampling the provided “waic” pointwise values to generate a standard error around the reported value?

 

Thanks.

 

Sent from Mail for Windows 10

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] WAIC
parts:
From a deterministic approximation to the posterior, there is only one
WAIC (beyond that there are at least two expressions for WAIC). Using a
MC approach, its valuable to know about the STDEV for the WAIC
estimate, I agree.
